data.long_meaning: Dhaya is a Sanskrit name meaning 'gift' or 'grace'. In Hindu mythology, it is the name of the goddess Dhaya Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth and prosperity. She is often depicted as holding a lotus flower and showering her blessings on her devotees. The name Dhaya carries the meaning “Gift, Grace” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Dhaya usually hope their child will grow to embody gift, grace and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Dhaya total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

historical_references.reference:
Dhaya Pancha Mahotsavam is a major festival celebrated in the temples dedicated to Lord Shiva in South India. It commemorates the five divine leelas, or acts, performed by Lord Shiva towards his consort Parvati. One of these acts is known as 'Dhaya' or 'Daya' which refers to the compassionate aspect of Lord Shiva, where he offered his third eye to Parvati to protect her from the demon Mohini.
Reference: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhaya_Pancha_Mahotsavam
Time_period: Ancient
Context: Hinduism, South India

Another reference to the name 'Dhaya' is in the context of the Hindu epic 'Ramayana'. Dhaya is the name of a sage who lived in the forest of Dandaka. He was a great devotee of Lord Rama and had attained the power of being able to revive the dead. Dhaya's act of kindness and compassion towards Rama and his brother Lakshmana after they had killed the demon Maricha is an example of the power of 'Dhaya' or 'compassion' in action.
Reference: https://www.jainworld.com/articles/sage-dhaya.html
Time_period: Ancient
Context: Hinduism, India
